terminal_bridge:
::: {.callout-chapter-connection title="From Trajectory Data to Supervised Adaptation"}
We have established how to diagnose agent failures, construct reproducible task fixtures, execute staged verification cascades, curate balanced recovery trajectories, and enforce strict structural split hygiene. However, a verified trajectory dataset stored on a distributed filesystem does not, by itself, alter model behavior. The raw tokens remain passive artifacts until they are compiled into loss functions and optimization objectives.

In Chapter 13 (*Supervised Adaptation*), we cross the boundary from data engineering to parameter optimization. We examine how to serialize heterogeneous trajectory graphs into sequence representations, design action-targeted loss masks that compute gradients exclusively over model-generated tokens while ignoring environment prompt context, pack variable-length execution paths into memory-efficient dense batches using block-diagonal attention masks, and optimize model parameters under the physical memory and bandwidth constraints of modern accelerator clusters.
:::
cumulative_ledger: Section 12.1 (Capability Gap Diagnosis): Before selecting policy adaptation, runtime engineers must rigorously diagnose whether an observed failure stems from an information deficit, an ambiguous tool interface, a runtime defect, or a true model capability deficit.

Section 12.2 (Task Fixture Design): Effective trajectory collection requires reproducible task fixtures—immutable starting environment states, pinned dependency versions, reset harnesses, and explicit mechanical completion criteria.

Section 12.3 (Staged Verifier Cascades): Raw trajectories must pass through an escalating verifier cascade from cheap mechanical checks to expensive semantic tests; acceptance proves satisfaction of specific checks, never omniscient correctness.

Section 12.4 (Recovery Demonstration Curation): Robust policies require curating three distinct behavioral categories: pristine expert demonstrations for forward efficiency, recovery traces for self-healing, and hard negative mining for error avoidance.

Section 12.5 (Collection Pipeline Architecture): An industrial trajectory harvesting pipeline requires asynchronous decoupled queues, isolated microVM sandboxes, strict backpressure governance, and resource-balanced stage provisioning.

Section 12.6 (Trajectory Provenance Tracking): Production trajectory datasets must maintain immutable cryptographic lineage (model snapshot, prompt hash, tool manifests, environment commit) while scrubbing sensitive credentials, API keys, and personal data.

Section 12.7 (Split Hygiene Verification): Trajectory dataset quality is validated only by measuring downstream task completion on strictly held-out environment fixtures, preventing subtle data leakage across task families.

Section 12.8 (End-to-End Trajectory Harvesting Synthesis): Industrial trajectory curation requires synthesizing reproducible fixtures, staged verification, recovery curation, and sanitization into a unified, versioned data pipeline evaluated against empirical yield and task transfer metrics.
